_doc: Bit-manipulation and integer-arithmetic techniques, expressed as VERIFIABLE CONTRACTS for oracle synthesis. Every entry gives an exact specification and a naive reference implementation that is obviously correct and slow -- the reference IS the oracle, and the fast form is the thing under test. Deliberately no optimised implementations: the system's job is to derive them and be checked, not to retrieve them. Inspired by the technique families surveyed in Hacker's Delight 2e (Warren, Addison-Wesley); registered for attribution at corpus/references/books/hackers_delight_2e.txt. No text or code from that book is reproduced here -- the contracts and references below are written independently, and these are long-standing published results.
why_these_matter: determinex_synthesize.py must REFUSE when it cannot derive a sound oracle, which is correct but limits how many tasks the verified-search loop can be demonstrated on. These functions are the opposite case: total functions on fixed-width integers, no environment dependence, with an exhaustively checkable domain at 8 and 16 bits. That makes the oracle sound BY CONSTRUCTION, so a solve rate measured on them cannot be explained away by a weak test.

verification_policy.u8: exhaustive over all 256 inputs -- a proof, not a sample
verification_policy.u32: structured sweep (0, 1, -1, all single-bit, all single-bit-pairs, powers of two and their neighbours, 0x55555555/0xAAAAAAAA/0x0F0F0F0F families) PLUS randomised trials against the reference
verification_policy.note: Report which policy was used. 'Passes 1,000 random u32 inputs' and 'exhaustive over u16' are different claims and must not be conflated.

entries.contract: popcount(x) returns the number of 1 bits in the fixed-width unsigned integer x.
entries.reference: def popcount(x, bits): return sum((x >> i) & 1 for i in range(bits))
entries.optimisation_class: divide-and-conquer bit-parallel accumulation; on most targets a single hardware instruction exists and the portable form is the fallback
edge_cases: all-ones -> bits
single bit set at every position

entries.contract: clz(x) returns the number of leading 0 bits in x. clz(0) is DEFINED here as the full width, because leaving it undefined is where portable implementations diverge from hardware ones.
entries.optimisation_class: binary search over bit positions, or float-exponent extraction
edge_cases: 0 -> bits (the case that most often disagrees with a hardware intrinsic)
1 -> bits-1
top bit set -> 0

entries.contract: ctz(x) returns the number of trailing 0 bits. ctz(0) is DEFINED here as the full width.
entries.reference:
def ctz(x, bits):
    if x == 0: return bits
    n = 0
    while (x >> n) & 1 == 0: n += 1
    return n
entries.optimisation_class: isolate lowest set bit (x & -x) then map to an index via de Bruijn multiply or popcount
edge_cases: 0 -> bits
only the top bit set -> bits-1

entries.contract: lowest_set(x) returns a value with only x's least-significant 1 bit set, or 0 when x is 0.
entries.optimisation_class: two's-complement identity on the whole word
edge_cases: powers of two map to themselves

entries.contract: clp2(x) returns the smallest power of two >= x, for x in [0, 2^(bits-1)]. clp2(0) is DEFINED as 1. Behaviour above 2^(bits-1) is OUT OF CONTRACT and must not be tested as if it were specified.
entries.reference:
def clp2(x, bits):
    if x <= 1: return 1
    p = 1
    while p < x: p <<= 1
    return p
entries.optimisation_class: smear the highest set bit downward, then increment
edge_cases: exact powers of two map to themselves, NOT to the next one -- the off-by-one that most implementations get wrong

entries.contract: is_pow2(x) is true iff x has exactly one bit set. Zero is NOT a power of two.
entries.reference: def is_pow2(x, bits): return sum((x >> i) & 1 for i in range(bits)) == 1
entries.optimisation_class: single mask-and-compare using the borrow behaviour of x-1
edge_cases: 0 -> false (the classic error: x & (x-1) == 0 alone says true)
1 -> true

entries.contract: reverse(x) returns x with its bit order reversed within the fixed width.
entries.optimisation_class: pairwise swap by masks at increasing strides
edge_cases: palindromic patterns map to themselves
reverse(reverse(x)) == x is a free property test

entries.contract: abs(x) for a SIGNED fixed-width integer. abs(INT_MIN) is OUT OF CONTRACT -- it is not representable, and a test asserting any particular value for it is testing an implementation choice rather than the specification.
entries.reference:
def sabs(x, bits):
    return -x if x < 0 else x
entries.optimisation_class: arithmetic-shift mask, add and xor -- no branch
edge_cases: INT_MIN -> undefined; the oracle must EXCLUDE it, and a synthesizer that silently includes it is producing an unsound test

entries.contract: avg(a, b) returns floor((a + b) / 2) computed WITHOUT the intermediate sum overflowing the fixed width.
entries.reference: def avg(a, b, bits): return (a + b) >> 1   # reference uses unbounded ints, so it cannot overflow
entries.optimisation_class: split into shared bits and differing bits so the sum never exceeds the width
edge_cases: both operands at the maximum -- the exact case a naive (a+b)>>1 gets wrong
operands differing by one, where floor matters

entries.contract: sign(x) returns -1 for x<0, 0 for x==0, +1 for x>0.
entries.optimisation_class: two shifts and an or, branchless
edge_cases: INT_MIN -> -1

entries.contract: has_zero_byte(w) is true iff any 8-bit lane of the fixed-width word is zero.
entries.reference: def has_zero_byte(w, bits): return any(((w >> (8*i)) & 0xFF) == 0 for i in range(bits // 8))
entries.optimisation_class: subtract-and-mask so all lanes are tested in one word operation -- the core of fast strlen/memchr
edge_cases: all lanes zero
no lane zero
zero only in the highest lane, where naive masks often produce a false negative

entries.contract: add_overflows(a, b) is true iff a+b is not representable in the SIGNED fixed width. Must be decided WITHOUT performing an operation that itself overflows.
entries.optimisation_class: sign comparison of operands against the sign of the truncated result
edge_cases: two large positives
two large negatives
opposite signs can NEVER overflow -- a check that flags them is wrong
